subject: Follow-up from ModelOps Live — PO C + next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@fluxdata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-20T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up from ModelOps Live — PO C + next steps

Hi Elena — great to meet you at ModelOps Live yesterday. Thanks for the quick demo of FluxData’s summarization pipeline — I wanted to capture a short recap and proposed next steps so we can move quickly if the priorities line up.

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary goal: reduce token costs for long-form customer documents while preserving summary fidelity.
- Scale: ~20M monthly tokens today, targeting 100M/mo in 6–9 months.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for interactive editor workflows; p99 target discussed for API endpoints.
- Constraints: data residency in US, procurement review, SOC2 evidence requested.

Proposed mutual action plan (draft)
1) Technical sync: 30-min call with your eng + our solutions engineer to align on sample corpus and latency profile (this week).
2) PO C (pilot): 3-week pilot with a small production slice (up to 1M tokens/day) to test cost/latency and evaluate caching/quantization.
3) Procurement & security: we’ll provide SOC2 and a short data handling FAQ; procurement review to run in parallel.
4) Decision: expand to Dedicated capacity or hosted commitment based on pilot results.

I attached a short draft mutual action plan (MAP-draft.pdf) and a 1‑page POC outline. Could you confirm the right stakeholders (eng, product, procurement) and a couple of windows that work for the technical sync?

Link to editable MAP: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-poc-outline

Thanks — happy to adjust scope if you want a smaller pilot first.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: MAP-draft.pdf (application/pdf, 145KB)
From: Elena Rossi <elena@fluxdata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from ModelOps Live — PO C + next steps

Hi Ben — thanks for the note and the recap — that’s exactly what we discussed. I’ve shared the MAP link with our engineering manager, Ryan, and procurement. A few clarifications from our side:

- Cost is a top constraint; we’re evaluating ways to reduce per-token spend while keeping model quality for legal-summary use cases.
- For latency, p95 is most important for the editor; p99 is nice-to-have for batch endpoints.
- Procurement will need a SSO/SOC2 package and a short data handling summary.

We can do the technical sync on Thursday 2026-02-26 between 10–11am PT or Friday 2026-02-27 after 1pm PT. I attached our standard SOW template so you can show mapping to your POC plan (SOW-template.docx).

Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Product | FluxData
elena@fluxdata.com

Attachment: SOW-template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 34KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@fluxdata.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-23T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from ModelOps Live — PO C + next steps

Thanks Elena — Thursday 2/26 10:30am PT works for Marissa and me. I’ve put a 30-min slot on the calendar (invite to follow).

POC outline (high-level)
- Week 0: onboarding, sample corpus ingestion, test dataset selection (Redwood provides ingestion scripts).
- Week 1–2: model tuning & deployment — experiment with batching, prefix caching, and a medium-quantized model variant to understand cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Week 3: evaluation on your quality prompts + cost reporting; handoff of findings and recommended config for scaled rollout.

Owners: Redwood SE (Marissa) will run the deployment + telemetry; Ben (me) will coordinate timelines and procurement deliverables; Rishi (cc’d) will support contract/commit questions at the leadership level.

I attached a slightly more detailed POC outline (redwood-poc-outline.pdf) and a shared checklist in the Drive. If procurement wants a tighter SOW, we can map the deliverables to your template.

See you on Thursday.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-03-05T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Quick check-in — POC timing / procurement status

Hi Elena — wanted to nudge this thread in case it fell off the radar. We’re ready to start the POC whenever you have alignment from procurement and eng. A couple quick options if useful:

- Start a focused 1-week feasibility spike (smaller scope) to unblock procurement and show cost/latency improvements quickly.
- Hold to the full 3-week pilot once procurement approves vendor onboarding.

If priorities changed and this isn’t a near-term focus, no problem — can you share expected timing (this month / next quarter / later)? Happy to align to your timeline.

Also — if procurement needs anything immediately, I can send SOC2 report and a short data handling FAQ.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Elena Rossi <elena@fluxdata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Chu <ryan.chu@fluxdata.com>, procurement@fluxdata.com
Date: 2026-03-06T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick check-in — POC timing / procurement status

Hi Ben — appreciate the follow-up. We’re still prioritizing internally; procurement has asked for vendor security docs and an internal data-handling summary before they greenlight any pilot. I’ve looped Ryan (engineering) and procurement on this thread — procurement@fluxdata.com will own the checklist.

Targeting late April for a pilot start at this point (we should know more by mid-March). Can you send SOC2 and a 1-page data handling summary to procurement directly? That will help accelerate the review.

Thanks,
Elena
